image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a male Mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The subject features a glossy iridescent green head, a distinct white neck ring, a yellow bill, and mottled brown/grey chest plumage. The background consists of rippling water with soft focus, and a partial view of another duck is visible in the upper left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with a characteristic yellow coloration consistent with a male Mallard.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, matching the biological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows dense, layered feather texture typical of waterproof plumage, and the posture indicates buoyancy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image perfectly matches the Mallard drake description: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and brownish-grey breast feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The duck is floating on water; legs and feet are submerged and completely occluded from view.
The wings are folded against the body and largely occluded by the angle and crop of the image; only the shoulder/covert area is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail section is outside the frame or obscured by the body angle; the characteristic curl is not visible.

AI models often blur this boundary or create a 'painted' look rather than distinct feather groups. Also, verify that the yellow bill has realistic texture (pores/lamellae) and isn't just a smooth plastic-like surface. Check the background duck for structural coherence—it should not be morphologically impossible even if blurry.
